subject: Marketplace tier minimums & channel margin experimentation
messages:
From: Michael López <m.lopez@terrahealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: TerraHealth Purchasing <purchasing@terrahealth.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Sep 2025 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: New marketplace ask — tier minimums and channel splits

Hi Hannah,

Quick one from our side as we map out the 2026 procurement plan. We're evaluating moving a portion of our Palo Alto deployment to marketplace/private-offer consumption. Our procurement and channel teams are pushing for two things: a) lower committed minimums for the first 12 months (we're talking a ~30% reduction on initial commit) and b) a clearly documented channel margin schedule so resellers know how to price against the marketplace offer.

Can Redwood share a sample tier/commit structure and expected channel netback examples? We want a short matrix so our commercial ops can model TCV and partner take. Happy to share rough volumes if that helps.

Thanks — Mike
Michael López
Head of Cloud Partnerships, TerraHealth
[Attachment: TH_initial_volumes.xlsx (spreadsheet)]
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Michael López <m.lopez@terrahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Sep 2025 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: New marketplace ask — tier minimums and channel splits

Mike — thanks for the clear ask and for sharing the volumes.

We can definitely put together a compact matrix that shows: list price, private-offer discount, reseller margin (pass-through and waterfall), and netback by tier. A couple of quick clarifying questions before we model scenarios:

- Are you prioritizing lower first-year commitment over long-term unit price, or is total 3-year TCV the main lens?
- Do you expect a single reseller to handle billing/implementation or multiple partners across regions?

Ben — looping you in to propose an experiment: instead of a single reduced minimum, what if we pilot two offer bands (low-commit starter band + performance kicker) and measure conversion vs. absolute ARR? Can you sketch a simple pricing experiment we could run with TerraHealth?

Irene — procurement will likely ask about invoice timing and listprice anchoring. Any redlines we should expect on payment cadence?

Happy to hop on a short call this week to walk through an initial matrix.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Michael López <m.lopez@terrahealth.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Sep 2025 10:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: New marketplace ask — tier minimums and channel splits

Mike / Hannah — appreciate the context. I sketched three experiment variants (summary below) — attaching a simple spreadsheet with netback math and sensitivity to commit/usage.

Experiment A — Starter band + standard reseller pass-through
- First-year minimum: 30% reduction vs standard PO floor
- Reseller margin: 18% flat on list
- Performance kicker: If usage > 125% of commit, additional 6% rebate applied retroactively

Experiment B — Low floor, shared upside
- First-year minimum: 50% reduction
- Reseller margin: 12% base + 4% shared upside if commit exceeded
- Longer-term renewal at blended list discount based on consumption

Experiment C — Anchor list price, longer-term lock
- No reduction to floor, but additional channel uplift (22%) for committed reseller exclusivity
- Better TCO for TerraHealth at 24+ month commit

Tradeoffs: A is quickest to approve (smaller netback impact), B is more attractive to customer but compresses reseller economics, C preserves reseller margin but asks for longer commitment.

Connor — can you confirm operational constraints (SKU mapping and metering) for a two-band pilot? If we need custom SKUs for the starter band, that will add ~2 weeks to enablement.

[Attachment: TH_private_offer_experiments.xlsx (spreadsheet)]
From: Michael López <m.lopez@terrahealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: TerraHealth Purchasing <purchasing@terrahealth.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Oct 2025 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: New marketplace ask — tier minimums and channel splits

Ben — this is super helpful, thank you. Procurement likes Experiment A and B but wants to avoid compressing reseller economics too much — they proposed a modified B: 40% first-year reduction, reseller margin 14% with a 3% shared upside. That gets us closer to their internal hurdle.

Two operational notes:
- We prefer a single reseller (CloudAxis) across our US accounts for simplicity.
- Invoice cadence must be monthly with a 30-day net; TerraHealth cannot accept accelerated upfront billing without a credit intermediation vehicle.

Can Redwood update the spreadsheet with the modified B and a short note we can include to CloudAxis outlining the reseller netback mechanics? If we can get that by COB Friday (10/3), we'll loop CloudAxis in.

— Mike
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Michael López <m.lopez@terrahealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Oct 2025 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: New marketplace ask — tier minimums and channel splits

Mike / team — quick confirmation on procurement constraints: monthly billing with NET30 is fine. We'll build the invoice timing into the private-offer terms and include a clause that the starter band converts to standard cadence on renewal.

Ben — I'll add a one-page note on 'reseller netback mechanics' for CloudAxis describing: list-price anchors, where the reseller margin sits relative to our private-offer discount, and the conditional performance kicker mechanics. Hannah — attaching the draft note and the modified spreadsheet.

Next steps agreed:
- Redwood to share updated modified-B spreadsheet & one-page reseller note by COB 2025-10-03.
- TerraHealth to confirm CloudAxis contact and greenlight for introduction.

Thanks — Irene
Irene Choi
Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
